headline: Jury convicts man of starting the deadly Palisades Fire
pages: A federal jury in Los Angeles on Friday convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, of starting the deadly 2025 Palisades Fire. His first federal trial earlier this year ended in a mistrial. Prosecutors said he lit a fire on Jan. 1, 2025, known as the Lachman Fire, that smoldered unseen in root systems before flaring back up on Jan. 7. That became one of the most destructive wildfires in California history, killing 12 people and destroying entire neighborhoods in Los Angeles and Malibu. He was found guilty of destruction of property by means of fire and of arson, after three days of deliberation. Bill Essayli, the top federal prosecutor in Los Angeles, praised his team's work.

Defense attorney Steve Haney said they were disappointed but respected the jury process, and that they would review appeal options. Sentencing is set for March 17, 2027, and each count carries a mandatory minimum. Why it matters: the verdict closes a major case tied to one of the state's worst disasters. Source: NPR.
